```plato

    //==
    // # Euler-Bernoulli beams
    //
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler%E2%80%93Bernoulli_beam_theory
    //
    // The 1D path over the `Beam` of `engineering.types.plato`, and the cheap
    // case whose answers can be checked: a cubic Hermite beam element reproduces
    // the exact deflected shape of a segment carrying no load between its ends,
    // so the deflections it reports AT THE NODES are exact — not converged-to,
    // exact — for point loads sitting on nodes, and for distributed loads too,
    // because the consistent load vector below is integrated rather than lumped.
    // Cantilever and simply-supported deflections come out equal to their
    // textbook closed forms to rounding.
    //
    // The model carries two degrees of freedom per node, transverse deflection
    // then rotation, and NO axial degree of freedom. Two consequences worth
    // stating: it cannot see axial force or buckling, and `Pinned` and `Roller`
    // restrain exactly the same thing here, since what distinguishes a roller is
    // the axial freedom this model does not have.
    //
    // Nodes are spaced uniformly and supports and point loads SNAP to the nearest
    // one. Choose an element count that lands a node on every support and every
    // point load — an even count on a symmetric span — or the analysis is of a
    // slightly different beam than the one described.

    // The bending stiffness EI, in newton-square-meters, about the section's Z
    // principal axis: the axis this transverse model bends about. A beam bending
    // about the other axis is the same beam with SecondMomentY and SecondMomentZ
    // exchanged in its section.
    BendingStiffness(b: Beam): Number
        => b.Material.YoungsModulus.Pascals * b.Section.SecondMomentZ;

    // The node stations of a uniform discretisation into `elementCount` elements:
    // elementCount + 1 stations from the beam's start to its end.
    BeamNodePositions(b: Beam, elementCount: Integer): Array<Length>
        => (elementCount + 1).MapRange(i =>
            Length(b.Length.Meters * i.ToNumber / elementCount.ToNumber));

    // The node nearest a station along the beam, clamped to the ends.
    BeamNearestNode(b: Beam, elementCount: Integer, position: Length): Integer
        => (position.Meters / b.Length.Meters * elementCount.ToNumber)
            .ToInteger.Clamp(0, elementCount);

    // The 4x4 element stiffness of one beam segment, row-major, over the degrees
    // of freedom (near deflection, near rotation, far deflection, far rotation).
    BeamElementStiffness(bendingStiffness: Number, elementLength: Number): Array<Number>
    {
        var l = elementLength;
        var c = bendingStiffness / (l * l * l);
        return [
            c * 12.0,      c * 6.0 * l,      -(c * 12.0),   c * 6.0 * l,
            c * 6.0 * l,   c * 4.0 * l * l,  -(c * 6.0 * l), c * 2.0 * l * l,
            -(c * 12.0),   -(c * 6.0 * l),   c * 12.0,      -(c * 6.0 * l),
            c * 6.0 * l,   c * 2.0 * l * l,  -(c * 6.0 * l), c * 4.0 * l * l];
    }

    // Every stiffness entry of the discretised beam, in global degree-of-freedom
    // numbering: element e owns degrees of freedom 2e through 2e + 3, so
    // consecutive elements share a node exactly as the coordinate list requires.
    BeamStiffnessEntries(b: Beam, elementCount: Integer): Array<SparseMatrixEntry>
    {
        var elementLength = b.Length.Meters / elementCount.ToNumber;
        var element = BeamElementStiffness(b.BendingStiffness, elementLength);
        return elementCount.Range.FlatMap(e =>
            16.MapRange(k => SparseMatrixEntry(e * 2 + k / 4, e * 2 + k % 4, element[k])));
    }

    // The degrees of freedom a support restrains, given that they are numbered
    // deflection first and rotation second: both for a Fixed end, the deflection
    // alone for Pinned and for Roller, none for Free. Pinned and Roller coincide
    // because this model carries no axial degree of freedom for a roller to
    // release.
    RestrainedDofCount(r: BeamRestraint): Integer
        => match (r)
        {
            Fixed => 2;
            Pinned => 1;
            Roller => 1;
            Free => 0;
        };

    // The prescribed displacements one support contributes: the first
    // `RestrainedDofCount` degrees of freedom of its node, each held at zero.
    BeamSupportConstraints(b: Beam, elementCount: Integer,
        support: BeamSupport): Array<PrescribedDisplacement>
    {
        var node = b.BeamNearestNode(elementCount, support.Position);
        return support.Restraint.RestrainedDofCount.MapRange(i =>
            PrescribedDisplacement(DofIndex(node * 2 + i), 0.0));
    }

    // Every essential boundary condition of the discretised beam.
    BeamConstraints(b: Beam, elementCount: Integer): Array<PrescribedDisplacement>
        => b.Supports.FlatMap(s => b.BeamSupportConstraints(elementCount, s));

    // The integral from 0 to x of the near-node DEFLECTION shape function, in the
    // element's unit parameter. This and the three below are the antiderivatives
    // of the cubic Hermite basis; they exist so that a distributed load covering
    // only PART of an element still produces its exact consistent nodal loads,
    // rather than a fraction of the full-element ones.
    HermiteNearDeflectionIntegral(x: Number): Number
        => x - x * x * x + x * x * x * x * 0.5;

    // The integral from 0 to x of the near-node ROTATION shape function, divided
    // by the element length.
    HermiteNearRotationIntegral(x: Number): Number
        => x * x * 0.5 - x * x * x * 2.0 / 3.0 + x * x * x * x * 0.25;

    // The integral from 0 to x of the far-node DEFLECTION shape function.
    HermiteFarDeflectionIntegral(x: Number): Number
        => x * x * x - x * x * x * x * 0.5;

    // The integral from 0 to x of the far-node ROTATION shape function, divided
    // by the element length.
    HermiteFarRotationIntegral(x: Number): Number
        => -(x * x * x / 3.0) + x * x * x * x * 0.25;

    // The consistent nodal loads of a uniform distributed force covering the unit
    // parameter range [from, to] of one element, in the order (near deflection,
    // near rotation, far deflection, far rotation). `magnitude` is the force per
    // unit length. Over a whole element these come out as the textbook
    // (wL/2, wL^2/12, wL/2, -wL^2/12).
    BeamDistributedElementLoads(magnitude: Number, elementLength: Number,
        from: Number, to: Number): Array<Number>
        => [
            magnitude * elementLength
                * (HermiteNearDeflectionIntegral(to) - HermiteNearDeflectionIntegral(from)),
            magnitude * elementLength * elementLength
                * (HermiteNearRotationIntegral(to) - HermiteNearRotationIntegral(from)),
            magnitude * elementLength
                * (HermiteFarDeflectionIntegral(to) - HermiteFarDeflectionIntegral(from)),
            magnitude * elementLength * elementLength
                * (HermiteFarRotationIntegral(to) - HermiteFarRotationIntegral(from))];

    // One element's share of a uniform distributed force spanning [start, end] in
    // meters along the beam. An element the load does not reach contributes four
    // zeros, because the clamped parameter range collapses to a point — so this
    // stays a map with no filtering step.
    BeamDistributedElementContributions(element: Integer, elementLength: Number,
        start: Number, end: Number, magnitude: Number): Array<DofLoad>
    {
        var origin = element.ToNumber * elementLength;
        var from = ((start - origin) / elementLength).Clamp(0.0, 1.0);
        var to = ((end - origin) / elementLength).Clamp(0.0, 1.0);
        var loads = BeamDistributedElementLoads(magnitude, elementLength, from, to);
        return 4.MapRange(k => DofLoad(DofIndex(element * 2 + k), loads[k]));
    }

    // A uniform distributed force resolved onto every element it covers.
    BeamDistributedContributions(b: Beam, elementCount: Integer, start: Length, end: Length,
        magnitude: Number): Array<DofLoad>
    {
        var elementLength = b.Length.Meters / elementCount.ToNumber;
        return elementCount.Range.FlatMap(e =>
            BeamDistributedElementContributions(e, elementLength, start.Meters, end.Meters,
                magnitude));
    }
```
